text:
irene: FYI — after the RBAC refactor we deployed at 02:45, several contractors report 403s on internal runbooks and CI dashboards. I’m seeing failed role assignment during SSO login.

sanjay: investigating. Alert spiked ~03:08 UTC, lots of SAML failures. Is this the employeeType change?

irene: yes — we split service.admin -> {service.admin, service.operator} and made JIT mapping require `employeeType` to pick operator/admin.

kevin: Okta logs show many assertions without `employeeType` (contractor orgs). Also getting intermittent KMS errors from saml-validator:
```
2026-03-20T03:09:12Z saml-validator ERROR decryptAssertion failed: KMSError: AccessDeniedException for key alias/redwood/saml-key
2026-03-20T03:09:12Z saml-validator DEBUG raw_assertion present, fallback -> unauthenticated_role
```

okta-bot: event: SAML_ASSERTION sent for user j.doe@thirdparty.co attributes: [email, groups, displayName] (employeeType: absent)

maria: So two independent failures: (1) missing attribute -> JIT can't map to operator/admin, (2) KMS decrypt denies causing validator to drop signature and fallback to default role. Together they cause 403s for resources that require explicit operator/admin.

sanjay: rolling back the RBAC refactor as a hotfix now (reverting mapping change) to restore access while we triage. Will post rollback job id.

kevin: thanks — I'm taking ownership of identity path. Immediate items: 1) Add tolerant JIT rule: if employeeType missing -> map to `contractor` (least privilege) not unauthenticated. 2) Patch saml-validator to retry KMS with alternate credential for key rotation windows. 3) Fix KMS key policy to include saml-validator role and Okta SAML service principal.

irene: rollback applied at 03:28 UTC, runbook access restored for affected teams. Confirming via impacted user. :white_check_mark:

kevin: quick fix PR for tolerant mapping opened: `identity/jit: default employeeType=contractor when absent` (link: https://git.redwood/identity/pulls/1298) — will canary to staging then prod.

maria: creating an incident (INC-2026-0319-01) to track RCA, postmortem, and audit logs. Need to capture: deploy that added the required attribute, KMS rotation job at 02:41, Okta metadata changes.

okta-bot: note: config change `require_employeeType_for_admin=true` toggled by infra-deploy at 02:45 by deployer-bot.

kevin: root cause summary draft: 1) RBAC refactor introduced hard requirement for `employeeType` in JIT mapping. 2) Several partner orgs do not provision `employeeType` attribute from Okta -> mapping fails. 3) KMS rotation/permission boundary caused saml-validator to intermittently drop assertion signatures -> fallback unauthenticated path. Combined effect: users without attribute and/or with dropped signature got unauthenticated or default viewer role leading to 403s.

sanjay: postmortem checklist: timeline, impacted user list, audit log export (SAML assertions, KMS errors), change owner (who toggled flag), and followups (identity, infra, SOC review).

maria: followups assigned: kevin (identity fixes + canary), infra (kms policy fix) — tagging @infra-team. Also require an audit alert rule for any future RBAC deploy that changes JIT required attributes.

irene: one more: double-check delegated-admins — there was at least one service account that lost admin perms due to mapping change, need emergency ACL update for paging.

kevin: noted — will add service account whitelist to JIT mapping to avoid future service-account lockouts.

maria: adding remediation ETA: identity fix by 2026-03-20 10:00 UTC, KMS policy fix by 2026-03-20 12:00 UTC, postmortem draft by EOD.

sanjay: closing the alert now since user access restored; keeping incident open for RCA. Thanks all. :handshake:
